history.period: 8th century CE origin; renovated 1448 by Rana Kumbha (reigned 1433-1468)
history.summary: Vaishnava temple inside Chittorgarh Fort on a raised plinth in Indo-Aryan style, with mandapa, ardha-mandapa, antarala, garbhagriha, pyramidal roof and a rare Garuda image under a canopy facing the temple. Originally dedicated to Vishnu as Varaha (an ancient Varaha image remains in the rear of the sanctum), with Krishna and Balarama consecrated later; sculptural evidence (Devi panels on the plinth) suggests it may originally have been a Shakti shrine before renovation by Maharana Kumbha in 1448, after whom it is named. SOURCE CONFLICTS: one source wrongly places it in Madhya Pradesh and claims Meera Bai married Rana Kumbha (she married Bhoj Raj in 1513; Kumbha died 1468). Coordinates approximate (complex-level).

name: Kumbha Shyam Temple
town_description: Chittorgarh, former capital of the Sisodia dynasty of Mewar, is dominated by its massive hill fort (a UNESCO World Heritage site), the largest fort in India, revered as a symbol of Rajput valour, sacrifice and devotion.

travel.railway: Chittorgarh Junction (~6 km from the fort)
travel.road: The temple is inside Chittorgarh Fort, ~350 m from Kumbha Palace, reached by the fort's hill road

visitor_information.opening_hours: Fort complex typically 6:00 AM-6:00 PM (fort entry ticket applies - verify)
